Tilt-Shift Diorama

Your product runs a tiny model town shot through a tilt-shift lens: a thin razor-sharp band, creamy blur everywhere else, boosted saturation and toy sunshine. Pulse is the teal van on patrol, and focus pulls to the one billboard that changed.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Diorama board — the town as low-poly boxes under a 35° perspective camera (not isometric)
  • Focus band — a gradient mask over a blurred duplicate — only a thin band stays sharp
  • Rooftop screens — billboards that show each metric's sparkline
  • Pulse van — a teal toy vehicle carrying the Acme mark — the agent on patrol
  • Tiny operator — a figure at a console with a big coral button — the human decision
  • Bokeh dots — defocused warm lights in the out-of-focus zones

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Focus pull — the sharp band slides to the subject, power2.inOut 0.8 s, arriving on the downbeat — it replaces cuts
  • Toy speed — vehicles and people move slightly fast on steps(12), which sells the miniature scale
  • Slow dolly — translateZ creep with layer parallax across the whole 8-bar phrase, linear, never on the beat

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Tilt-shift makes any system look small, legible and under control — exactly the feeling of a background watcher — and the focus band is a built-in attention pointer. Risk: the blur limits copy to the focus band; overlay type must sit on calm, defocused areas.

Adapt to your product: Build your product's world as a model town (services as buildings, users as figures, your agent as the vehicle) and put your one key alert on the billboard where focus lands.
